public_task_requirement: Please implement a website for a credit repair company to generate leads. The website should have a form-filling function, allowing users to input personal information and credit status. The website should also have a credit score inquiry function and an introduction to credit repair services. Users can browse the website, learn about credit repair services, and fill out the form to submit lead information. Set old lace as the body background and use rosy brown for the UI.

task_summary.requirement_coverage: The site targeted a credit repair lead-generation landing page with three core user-facing capabilities: a form for personal/credit-status lead capture, a credit score inquiry action, and an introduction to credit repair services, all styled with an old lace body background and rosy brown UI. Verified strengths: the credit score inquiry flow was observed to work and display a score/feedback; the color palette was judged to match the requested scheme; the page rendered without visible runtime errors. Main functional risks: the lead form was not confirmed as submitted before interaction budget exhaustion, so the confirmation state was not reached; the services/introduction content was not fully verified and was reported as not found in the interaction trace; navigation/content visibility depended on switching views, which limited confirmation of the required landing-page coverage. Visible observations: the homepage showed navigation buttons, a credit score CTA, and a lead form view existed in the implementation, but the evaluator’s screenshot-based review noted that the first screen did not visibly present all required sections together.
verified_strengths: Credit score inquiry was confirmed to display a score and qualitative feedback after the inquiry button was used.
The requested old lace background and rosy brown UI styling were observed as matching the specification.
The page rendered cleanly with no visible errors in the evaluation evidence.
primary_functional_risks: Form submission was not reached, so the lead-recording confirmation state remains unverified.
The credit repair services introduction was not confirmed during interaction and was reported as absent/not found in the evaluated flow.
Because the site uses separate views, required content may not be visible until navigation occurs, increasing the risk that the landing experience does not satisfy the lead-gen brief immediately.
primary_visual_observations: The landing page showed navigation and a credit score CTA, but the screenshot-based review said the form-filling function and detailed services introduction were not visibly present on the first screen.
The color scheme was observed as compliant, but the text contrast on the hero area was noted as low in the appearance evaluator output.

appearance_reflection.observed_result: The home view renders a single heading, "Welcome to Credit Repair Experts." The heading sits inside a white card on top of the oldlace page background, and the page also uses rosybrown for the navigation bar and buttons. The reviewer reported that the text contrast is very low and that the typography is minimal, with font weight or contrast needing improvement for readability.
appearance_reflection.likely_cause_or_limitation: The screenshot-based appearance issue is supported by the rendered styling: the page uses light text defaults from the global stylesheet together with a light background and simple typography choices. This is an appearance problem, not a missing feature.
appearance_reflection.preventative_action: Use text and heading styles that keep the main headline and body copy clearly readable against the page background, and give headings and body text enough weight or contrast to pass a quick first-screen readability check.
appearance_reflection.verification: On the rendered first screen, the main headline and body text should be readable at a glance without squinting, and the text should remain clearly legible against the background.
appearance_reflection.transfer_limits: Applies to lead-generation landing pages and other single-page marketing sites that rely on a prominent headline and short supporting copy.

evidence_refs.same_fix: Increase the heading and body text contrast and adjust typography weight so the text is easier to read.

appearance_reflection.deduction: the contrast between the text ("Welcome to Credit Repair Experts") and the background is very low, making the text hard to read || the typography is minimal but could use some improvements in font weight or contrast for better readability
appearance_reflection.group_reason: Increase the heading and body text contrast and adjust typography weight so the text is easier to read.

functional_reflections.user_trigger: After entering valid personal and credit-status information in the lead form, the user submits the form.
functional_reflections.expected_state_change: The page shows a submission confirmation message indicating the lead information was received and that someone will contact the user.
functional_reflections.observed_result: The tester filled in the form fields and selected a credit issue, but did not click the submit button, so no confirmation message appeared.
functional_reflections.likely_cause_or_limitation: (unverified against code) The check ended before the final submit action, so the form’s success state was never triggered. This is a tester limitation rather than a website defect.
functional_reflections.preventative_action: For any form with a submit button, keep the submit control clearly reachable and wire it to a visible success state that replaces or follows the form after submission. The confirmation should be rendered by the form’s submit handler so users immediately see that their entry was accepted.
functional_reflections.verification: Click the submit button after filling the required fields; the page should switch to the success message section defined by the form component.
functional_reflections.transfer_limits: This reflection only covers the lead form submission confirmation flow. It does not evaluate the credit score inquiry or services browsing features.

investigation.task: The check’s task was to fill out the lead form and submit it so the site shows a confirmation that the lead information was recorded. The tester’s final answer says PARTIAL because the submission button was never clicked, so the expected post-submit state was not reached.
investigation.reached_target: The tester did reach the form page and entered personal information, but did not complete the target action of submitting the form. The trajectory ends at the filled form with the tester explicitly stating they had not clicked the submission button.
investigation.screenshots: The screenshots show the form page with First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone Number, and the credit issue dropdown filled or focused, but no confirmation message is visible. The submit button is not visible in the captured area, so the expected success state is not shown.
investigation.code_path: src/App.vue contains the Get Started navigation and mounts FormView when currentView === 'form'; src/views/FormView.vue contains the form and a submit handler that sets submitted.value = true and conditionally renders the success message. The route/component chain exists, so the feature is present in code and the missing confirmation is not due to an absent page.
investigation.style_trace: not applicable; the code includes the success message branch, but the screenshots do not show the post-submit state and the tester never clicked submit, so there is no rendered confirmation to trace through styles.
investigation.candidates: 1) Tester limitation: supported by the trajectory and final answer, which say the submission button was never clicked. 2) Missing feature: ruled out by src/views/FormView.vue, which does render a success-message section after submit. 3) Styling/visibility issue: not supported, because no post-submit state was reached to inspect.
investigation.conclusion: The surviving cause is that the check stopped before the final submit action, so the confirmation state was never triggered. The website’s form submit handler exists and would show the success message after submission, but this run did not exercise it.
investigation.fix_check: No code change is required for this specific failure; the tester needed one more interaction to click the submit button. If a code change were needed for similar cases, it would be in src/views/FormView.vue to keep the submit button reachable and ensure the submit handler flips the submitted state.

investigation.reached_target: The tester did reach the form page and entered personal information, but did not complete the target action of submitting the form. The trajectory ends at the filled form with the tester explicitly stating they had not clicked the submission button.
investigation.screenshots: The screenshots show the form page with First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone Number, and the credit issue dropdown filled or focused, but no confirmation message is visible. The submit button is not visible in the captured area, so the expected success state is not shown.
investigation.code_path: src/App.vue contains the Get Started navigation and mounts FormView when currentView === 'form'; src/views/FormView.vue contains the form and a submit handler that sets submitted.value = true and conditionally renders the success message. The route/component chain exists, so the feature is present in code and the missing confirmation is not due to an absent page.
investigation.style_trace: not applicable; the code includes the success message branch, but the screenshots do not show the post-submit state and the tester never clicked submit, so there is no rendered confirmation to trace through styles.
investigation.candidates: 1) Tester limitation: supported by the trajectory and final answer, which say the submission button was never clicked. 2) Missing feature: ruled out by src/views/FormView.vue, which does render a success-message section after submit. 3) Styling/visibility issue: not supported, because no post-submit state was reached to inspect.
investigation.conclusion: The surviving cause is that the check stopped before the final submit action, so the confirmation state was never triggered. The website’s form submit handler exists and would show the success message after submission, but this run did not exercise it.
investigation.fix_check: No code change is required for this specific failure; the tester needed one more interaction to click the submit button. If a code change were needed for similar cases, it would be in src/views/FormView.vue to keep the submit button reachable and ensure the submit handler flips the submitted state.

task_summary.requirement_coverage: The site targeted a credit repair lead-generation landing page with three core user-facing capabilities: a form for personal/credit-status lead capture, a credit score inquiry action, and an introduction to credit repair services, all styled with an old lace body background and rosy brown UI. Verified strengths: the credit score inquiry flow was observed to work and display a score/feedback; the color palette was judged to match the requested scheme; the page rendered without visible runtime errors. Main functional risks: the lead form was not confirmed as submitted before interaction budget exhaustion, so the confirmation state was not reached; the services/introduction content was not fully verified and was reported as not found in the interaction trace; navigation/content visibility depended on switching views, which limited confirmation of the required landing-page coverage. Visible observations: the homepage showed navigation buttons, a credit score CTA, and a lead form view existed in the implementation, but the evaluator’s screenshot-based review noted that the first screen did not visibly present all required sections together.
verified_strengths: Credit score inquiry was confirmed to display a score and qualitative feedback after the inquiry button was used.
The requested old lace background and rosy brown UI styling were observed as matching the specification.
The page rendered cleanly with no visible errors in the evaluation evidence.
primary_functional_risks: Form submission was not reached, so the lead-recording confirmation state remains unverified.
The credit repair services introduction was not confirmed during interaction and was reported as absent/not found in the evaluated flow.
Because the site uses separate views, required content may not be visible until navigation occurs, increasing the risk that the landing experience does not satisfy the lead-gen brief immediately.
primary_visual_observations: The landing page showed navigation and a credit score CTA, but the screenshot-based review said the form-filling function and detailed services introduction were not visibly present on the first screen.
The color scheme was observed as compliant, but the text contrast on the hero area was noted as low in the appearance evaluator output.

appearance_reflection.observed_result: On the first screen shown, the landing page does not visibly present the form-filling function and the credit repair services introduction together; the screenshot-based review specifically noted that the form-filling function was not clearly visible and the services introduction was not visible in the initial view.
appearance_reflection.likely_cause_or_limitation: The implementation appears to split content across separate views, so the landing screen only shows navigation and a credit score CTA instead of surfacing all required lead-generation sections at once.
appearance_reflection.preventative_action: Show the form-filling section, the credit score inquiry control, and a visible credit repair services introduction on the landing page first screen.
appearance_reflection.verification: Open the homepage and confirm that the initial viewport contains readable lead form fields, the credit score inquiry entry/control, and introductory credit repair service content without requiring navigation or scrolling.
appearance_reflection.transfer_limits: This reflection is limited to what was visible in the supplied screenshot and evaluator notes; it does not claim the hidden form or services content is broken, only that it was not visible on the first screen.

appearance_reflections.observed_result: The home view renders a single heading, "Welcome to Credit Repair Experts." The heading sits inside a white card on top of the oldlace page background, and the page also uses rosybrown for the navigation bar and buttons. The reviewer reported that the text contrast is very low and that the typography is minimal, with font weight or contrast needing improvement for readability.
appearance_reflections.likely_cause_or_limitation: The screenshot-based appearance issue is supported by the rendered styling: the page uses light text defaults from the global stylesheet together with a light background and simple typography choices. This is an appearance problem, not a missing feature.
appearance_reflections.preventative_action: Use text and heading styles that keep the main headline and body copy clearly readable against the page background, and give headings and body text enough weight or contrast to pass a quick first-screen readability check.
appearance_reflections.verification: On the rendered first screen, the main headline and body text should be readable at a glance without squinting, and the text should remain clearly legible against the background.
appearance_reflections.transfer_limits: Applies to lead-generation landing pages and other single-page marketing sites that rely on a prominent headline and short supporting copy.
